chunks.title: FoodCycler FC-50 Specifications
chunks.content: 120V, 60Hz, 500W max appliance measuring 14.2"H x 12.6"D x 11.0"W, weighing ~20 lbs, with ~10.5 cup (2.5L) capacity and ~4-8 hour processing time.

chunks.title: Electrical Safety - Grounded Outlet Only
chunks.content: Always use a grounded outlet; never remove the ground, use an adapter, extension cord, or plug into a timer/switch-controlled outlet, as failure to follow this can cause death or electrical shock.

scenarios.condition: Setting up or plugging in the appliance
steps: Use only a grounded wall outlet
Never remove the ground pin or use an adapter
Never use an extension cord or timer/switch-controlled outlet
If the plug won't fit, contact a qualified electrician instead of modifying it

chunks.title: Never Immerse in Liquid
chunks.content: Never put the power cord, power plug, or base in water or other liquid, and never pour liquid over the appliance to clean; if the appliance becomes submerged, unplug immediately.

scenarios.condition: Appliance contacts or is submerged in liquid
steps: Unplug the appliance immediately
Do not touch the appliance while it may be energized
Contact Vitamix Customer Service before further use

chunks.title: Blades Are Extremely Sharp
chunks.content: Never manually clean or come into contact with the blades, and never put hands inside the appliance unless a cycle has completely finished, and the unit is off and unplugged.

steps: Turn off and unplug the appliance
Remove the bucket from the base before touching contents
Never reach inside the bucket while installed in the appliance
Never manually clean the blades

chunks.title: Hot Surfaces - Cooling Period Required
chunks.content: Never touch hot surfaces; always use product handles, and allow FoodCycler components to cool approximately 35 minutes after a cycle completes before opening the lid.

chunks.title: Never Open Lid or Remove Bucket During Operation
chunks.content: Never open the lid or remove the bucket during a cycle; ensure the cycle is complete and the appliance is unplugged before removing the bucket.

chunks.title: Fill Line and Overloading
chunks.content: Never add food waste above the thin, indented fill line inside the bucket or pack food down to keep it below the line, since overloading can cause the appliance to jam.

chunks.title: Remove Bucket Before Adding Waste
chunks.content: Always remove the bucket before adding food waste to ensure it goes into the bucket and not the main body, which could damage the motor and internal components; never add waste directly without the bucket installed.

chunks.title: No Foreign Objects or Prohibited Materials
chunks.content: Never leave foreign objects (spoons, forks, knives) in the bucket, and never process large bones, pits, candy, gum, nuts, or hard shells as these can damage the blades or cause motor overload.

chunks.title: No Oil, Flammables, or Water; No Ingesting By-product
chunks.content: Never add oil, flammable materials, compounds, or water to the FoodCycler, and never consume or ingest plant food or food waste placed in the bucket.

chunks.title: Authorized Parts and Filters Only
chunks.content: Never use attachments, carbon filters, or lids not sold/authorized by Vitamix, and never let anyone other than Vitamix or an authorized service representative repair or service the unit; unauthorized parts or repairs void the warranty.

chunks.title: Storage and Operating Environment
chunks.content: Never place the appliance near a hot burner, oven, or heater, never store or use it outdoors exposed to sunlight or freezing temperatures, and operate it in the 68-82.4°F (20-28°C) range with adequate ventilation.

chunks.title: Household Use Only
chunks.content: This product is intended for household use only and is not intended for commercial purposes; commercial use is a misuse that can void the warranty.

chunks.title: Parts and Features Overview
chunks.content: The FC-50 includes a main body with processing lid, two replaceable carbon filters, a bucket that grinds/processes waste, a bucket lid with pre-loaded filter, carbon filter caps, a removable back panel, and a power cord.

chunks.title: Before First Use Setup
chunks.content: Remove all packaging, plug cover, and promotional labels; open the lid by rotating counterclockwise; remove filter caps and plastic wrap; remove paper rings from bucket top and bottom; discard the max-fill sticker and vent sticker inside the bucket compartment; optionally apply the French sticker overlay; release the back panel, return white stickers to filter locations, install filter caps with half-moon opening toward the back panel, and reinstall the back panel.

chunks.title: What You Can and Cannot Process
chunks.content: Most fruit/veggie scraps, beans, meat, fish, poultry, coffee grounds, cereals, pet food, eggs, and poultry/fish bones are fine; fibrous items and whole fruits/veggies should be cut up; dairy, jams, sauces, and starches only in small amounts; oils, paper products, coffee pods, cardboard/glass/wood/metal, candy, large bones, and hard pits should never be processed.

rows: Most fruit & veggie scraps, beans/seeds/legumes, meat/fish/shellfish/poultry scraps, coffee grounds/filters/tea bags, cereals & grains, pet food, eggs & shells, poultry & fish bones
Fibrous herbs, citrus fruit rinds, corn cobs & husks, whole fruits & vegetables, celery/asparagus & other fibrous plants
Dairy products, jellies/jams/puddings, starches (bread, cake, rice), sauces/soups/dressings/gravies
Oils & fats, paper towel or tissue, coffee pods, candy & gum, cardboard/glass/wood/metal, large beef/pork/lamb bones, pineapple leaves, hard pits (peach, apricot, lychee, mango, avocado)

chunks.title: Loading and Starting a Cycle
chunks.content: Open the lid, remove the bucket, add food waste up to the fill line, reinsert the bucket aligning the arrows, close and lock the lid, plug in the appliance (it enters STANDBY), and press On/Off once to start; the cycle runs Drying, Grinding, and Cooling modes for about 4-8 hours.

chunks.title: Completing a Cycle and Removing By-product
chunks.content: The appliance beeps when the cycle completes and stays in Standby up to 30 minutes; unplug it once all lights are off, wait ~35 minutes for cooling, then open the lid and remove the bucket.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Appliance Exterior
chunks.content: Wipe the outside surface and bucket compartment with a wrung-out cloth dampened with mild soap and water only, then dry with a clean towel; recommended every 3-4 months.

chunks.title: Cleaning the Bucket
chunks.content: Empty the bucket and wipe residue with a paper towel, then place it in the lower dishwasher rack (allow to cool if using a hot cycle) or hand-wash with warm water and dish soap, scrubbing around and beneath the grinding arms.

chunks.title: Replacing the Carbon Filters
chunks.content: When the Change Filter light illuminates, release the back panel, remove filter caps, unscrew filters counter-clockwise, install new filters (threaded end down, rotate clockwise until it stops), reattach caps with half-moon opening toward the back panel, and reset the indicator manually if needed by pressing the round button until it beeps.

chunks.title: Replacing the Bucket Lid Filter
chunks.content: When bucket odors become unpleasant, remove the bucket lid, take off the wingnut and slotted metal plate, remove and discard the old filter (do not wash it), install the new filter, plate, and wingnut, then return the lid to the bucket.

chunks.title: Using the By-product as Plant Food
chunks.content: Mix the by-product into soil at 1:10 (or 1:15 for cycles heavy in animal protein), never apply it directly to the soil surface, and wait 1-4 weeks before planting; it can also be discarded in a green bin or garbage can per local regulations.

chunks.title: Manual Reset Procedure
chunks.content: To reset the operating system: plug in the appliance, press and hold On/Off for 3 seconds until it beeps and powers down, unplug for 1 minute, plug back in and wait 10 seconds, then press On/Off to restart; repeat if it doesn't work the first time.

chunks.title: On/Off Button and Lid Sensor Issues
chunks.content: An unlit On/Off button usually means STANDBY mode or a power connection issue; a flashing button with beeps indicates the lid is unlocked or the sensor is dislodged.

rows: Appliance may be in STANDBY (no action needed); verify power cord is connected at both ends; unplug and replug; contact Vitamix if it persists
On/Off button is flashing and audible beeps
Lid is unlocked or sensor is dislodged; lock the lid and contact Vitamix if it continues

chunks.title: Drying Light Flashing Causes and Fixes
chunks.content: A flashing Drying light can indicate food waste in the main body, an overloaded bucket, oversized food waste, or a grinding arm issue; each requires unplugging, cooling 35 minutes, and inspecting/clearing the bucket before restarting.

rows: Food waste is in the main body
Unplug, cool 35 min, remove bucket, remove waste from main body
Unplug, cool 35 min, remove bucket, manually turn gear underneath counter-clockwise, remove waste below fill line, reinstall and restart
Unplug, cool 35 min, remove bucket, remove and cut waste smaller, reinstall and restart
Unplug, cool 35 min, remove bucket, manually turn gear counter-clockwise; if it hesitates or won't turn, contact Vitamix

chunks.title: Other Light and Cosmetic Issues
chunks.content: Grinding, Cooling, or all lights flashing together indicate a machine issue requiring Vitamix support; faded or chipped bucket coating is cosmetic only and does not affect function.

rows: Grinding, Cooling, or All lights flashing
Machine issue; contact Vitamix Customer Service
Bucket coating is faded or chipped
Not a defect; cosmetic wear from food scraping, does not affect function

chunks.title: Warranty Voiding Conditions
chunks.content: Abuse, misuse, negligent use, alteration, exposure to extreme conditions, failure to follow instructions, unauthorized repairs, or using non-Vitamix components voids the warranty.

tasks.title: Complete Pre-Use Setup Steps
tasks.description: Unbox the unit, remove packaging/rings/stickers, and prepare the filters and back panel before first use.
tasks.justification: Skipping setup steps like removing the max-fill sticker or paper rings can cause the appliance to malfunction or jam on first use.
tasks.instructions_text: Remove all packaging, the plug cover, and promotional labels. Open the lid by rotating counterclockwise to the unlock symbol and lift off. Remove filter caps and plastic wrap, then pull the bucket out and remove paper rings from both the top and bottom of the bucket. Discard the max-fill sticker and the vent sticker inside the bucket compartment. Release the back panel, return the white stickers to their filter locations, install the filter caps with the half-moon opening facing the back panel, and snap the back panel back into place.

tasks.title: Wipe Down Appliance Exterior and Compartment
tasks.description: Clean the outer surfaces and bucket compartment of the FoodCycler with a damp cloth.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic only — keeps the appliance surfaces free of residue and grime, recommended every 3-4 months.
tasks.instructions_text: Using a wrung-out cloth dampened with mild soap and water, wipe down the outside surfaces and around the bucket compartment. Dry any remaining moisture with a clean towel.

tasks.title: Clean the Bucket
tasks.description: Empty and wash the processing bucket after use to remove food residue and prevent odor buildup.
tasks.justification: Leaving residue in the bucket can cause odors and attract pests, though it does not affect the grinding mechanism itself.
tasks.instructions_text: Remove all material from the bucket and wipe out residue with a paper towel. Place the bucket in the lower rack of the dishwasher, or hand-wash with warm water and a small amount of dish soap, scrubbing around and beneath the grinding arms. Let the bucket cool before handling if you used a hot dishwasher cycle.

tasks.title: Replace Carbon Filters
tasks.description: Swap out the two carbon filters when the Change Filter indicator lights up or odors persist.
tasks.justification: Worn-out carbon filters can no longer wick away odors, and continuing to run the appliance without replacing them defeats their odor-control function.
tasks.instructions_text: Release the back panel and remove the filter caps. Turn each filter counter-clockwise to remove it, then install new filters with the threaded end facing down, rotating clockwise until they stop turning. Reinstall the filter caps with the half-moon opening facing the back panel, and reinstall the back panel. If the Change Filter light doesn't reset automatically, press and hold the small round button until it beeps.

tasks.title: Replace Bucket Lid Filter
tasks.description: Replace the filter inside the bucket lid when bucket odors become unpleasant.
tasks.justification: An exhausted lid filter stops containing food scrap odors during counter-top collection.
tasks.instructions_text: Remove the bucket lid, flip it over, and remove the wingnut and slotted metal plate. Remove and discard the old filter, then install the new filter, replace the metal plate, and reattach the wingnut. Return the lid to the bucket.

tasks.title: Run a Citrus-Only Cycle to Mitigate Odors
tasks.description: Occasionally run a cycle using only citrus rinds to help refresh the carbon filters and reduce odors.
tasks.justification: The manual states this helps mitigate filter odors and extend filter usability between replacements.
tasks.instructions_text: Load the bucket with only citrus rinds such as lemons or oranges up to the fill line, then run a normal processing cycle as usual.

tasks.title: Unplug When Not in Use to Extend Filter Life
tasks.description: Turn off and unplug the appliance between uses rather than leaving it in Active mode.
tasks.justification: The manual states leaving the appliance in Active mode reduces carbon filter life.
tasks.instructions_text: After a cycle finishes and the appliance has cooled, unplug it from the power outlet until you are ready to start the next cycle.

weekly.title: Routine Care
steps: Empty and wipe out the bucket with a paper towel after each cycle
Dishwasher-safe (lower rack) or hand-wash the bucket with warm water and dish soap, scrubbing around the grinding arms
Wipe down the appliance exterior and bucket compartment with a damp cloth every 3-4 months

deep_clean.title: Filter Replacement
steps: Release the back panel to access carbon filters
Remove filter caps and unscrew old filters counter-clockwise
Install new filters threaded-end down, rotating clockwise until they stop
Reinstall filter caps (half-moon opening toward back panel) and the back panel
Reset the Change Filter indicator manually if it doesn't clear automatically
Remove and replace the bucket lid filter when odors persist, discarding the old filter without washing it

warranty.coverage: Vitamix warrants the Food Recycler (motor base, bucket, and lid purchased together) for household use against defects in material or workmanship and normal wear and tear for 3 years from purchase/delivery date; Vitamix will repair, replace, or refund the purchase price at its discretion.
exclusions: cosmetic changes like discoloration or effects of abrasives/cleaners or food buildup
worn or chipped coating on inner wall or floor of bucket
